relevance_note: Cohort of 13 participants with LAMP2 mutations, each described individually in tables: "Thirteen participants (5 males and 8 females) with genetically confirmed LAMP2 mutations were enrolled to the study."
method_note: Read the whole paper; built the JSON with a Python script that parses Tables I-III and asserts every span occurs verbatim; table-derived values were checked against the tables by hand. Labels: participants use the paper's '#n' form (text: 'patient #1', 'Patient#5', '(#1)'; tables: '# 1', '# 1/M'). No variant descriptions are printed (only 'Splicing' / 'Stop codon' in Table II), so every variant row has variant_original_string 'not reported'. Zygosity comes from the Discussion statement about the sample ('hemizygous males ... heterozygous females'). Inheritance for #1 combines 'his mother (patient #2)' with 'Patients #1-8 ... had the same splice site mutation'; for #5 from 'His asymptomatic mother (patient #6) was found to be a carrier of the kindred's mutation'. Age at onset is Table II 'Age at clinical presentation (y)'. Table II medical-comorbidity abbreviations are expanded from its legend; 'CPK' there is read as an elevated value only for the checklist (legend: 'CPK, creatinine phosphokinase'). 'Impaired LFT' is not mapped to the transaminase checklist item unless the text says hypertransaminasemia (#1, #3, #5); 'CMP' and 'Hypertrophy' (#9) are not mapped to LVH; only 'hypertrophic cardiomyopathy' is. Intellectual disability is excluded for the 11 other participants with an FSIQ from 'Of the 12 participants that completed FSIQ assessment ... only one patient ... (patient #12)' (#4 had FSIQ NA); this does not exclude the composite checklist item except for #5 ('no signs of cognitive impairment'). Borderline intelligence (#3, #6) is recorded as a feature but not mapped to the checklist. 'None' in the psychiatric-comorbidity or medical-comorbidity columns, 'did not manifest any of the classical features of Danon disease' (#2, #4, #6) and 'No ophthalmological abnormalities were reported in this cohort' are recorded as broad excluded features only, without excluding specific checklist items (D-27). Relatives: the kindred's first grandparent (Kariv et al., 1971), labelled 'great-grandfather of #1' from 'Patient #1 is his great-grandson'; #2's two brothers (#1's uncles), ordered as mentioned so 'brother of #2' is the one who died after heart transplantation and 'brother of #2 2' the one who died of sudden arrhythmia (assignment by order of mention, age at death 'around 35 y'); #5's grandmother. 'Two of his grandchildren died with the same phenotype at age 35 y' (kindred paragraph) probably refers to #2's brothers but the paper does not say so; no separate rows were created for them. #5's 'non-affected younger brother' is untested and unaffected, so out of scope. Previously published people with individual facts: the two Danon et al. (1981) boys, and the Hatz 2010, Tanidir 2015 and Sugie 2016 cases; Sugie 2002 and Boucek 2011 are group-level only. Families 1-5 belong to one Israeli kindred (Table II legend). Contradictions: (1) text says panic disorder n = 1, but Table II lists panic disorder for #8 and #10 (and #10's text confirms it); (2) #1's molecular diagnosis is 'at age 10', but the case report implies the LAMP2 finding followed events 'At the age of 12 y'; (3) #10's Table II clinical presentation is 23, while the text says cardiomyopathy was diagnosed at 19 and the DD mutation at 23; (4) #3 is listed with Medications 'None' while the text mentions starting Ritalin for ADHD at 6 years; (5) Table III EF for #5 is printed '-.1.10'. No stacked cells in this paper.
